body:
Part of #2390, related to #2349 / #2350.

## Problem

Rich chat content (inline images, media actions, attachments) is built on main-only, local reads. Over Annex, every one of those reads would either fail or, worse, resolve against the controller's own disk. Pasting an image to a remote chat agent today silently loses it.

## Established (origin/main 91da2bc6)

- Media is stored on the satellite by reference: `chat-media.ts:1-15` stores images as `<agent transcript dir>/media/<sha256>.<ext>` and keeps only the ref in events; "The renderer asks for media by reference, never by path."
- `IPC.CHAT.READ_MEDIA` (`chat-handlers.ts:184-190`) reads from the local media dir, gated by the controller's own `richChatContent` flag (`assertRichMedia`). `MEDIA_ACTION` `'reveal'` calls `shell.showItemInFolder(mediaFilePath(agentId, mediaRef))` on the local machine (`chat-handlers.ts:192-198`).
- Attachments: `STAGE_ATTACHMENT` (`chat-handlers.ts:168-182`) stages a controller-local file path or bytes into the local agent's staging area; `SEND_MESSAGE` resolves staged ids locally (`:155`). The Annex message route (`annex-server.ts:1710-1745`) takes text only.
- `clipboard:image` over WS (`annex-server.ts:2309-2322` → `handleClipboardImage`, `:333-372`) writes a temp file on the satellite and pastes its path into the PTY with `ptyManager.write`. For a chat agent that write is a no-op (`pty-manager.ts:549-551`), no error is sent back, and the temp file stays for 30 minutes.
- Rich link tokens call `git.githubRepo(dirPath)` (`rich/github-ref-client.ts:60`) with a directory path; for a remote agent that path belongs to the satellite.

## Proposed approach

- Satellite route `GET /api/v1/agents/:id/chat/media/:mediaRef` (authenticated, read-only). It validates `mediaRef` with the same `mediaRefArg` / `isMediaRef` rules, resolves only inside the agent's media dir, and returns bytes with the sniffed MIME type and the existing size cap. The satellite's `richChatContent` flag gates it.
- Controller: `chat.readMedia` for a remote agent id goes to that route; `mediaAction 'reveal'` is hidden for remote agents; `'copy'` copies the fetched bytes.
- Attachments: the controller stages bytes (never a path) and uploads them with the message: extend the chat send route with `attachments: [{ name, mimeType, base64 }]`, capped like `clipboard:image` (10 MB) and `CHAT_ATTACHMENTS_MAX`. The satellite stages them through `stageAttachmentData` and checks the agent's capabilities.
- `clipboard:image` for a chat agent: return an `error` (for example `chat_agent_use_attachments`) and write nothing, until the attachment path exists.
- Rich links and file chips for remote agents must not call any controller-local path API with a satellite path. Either resolve them on the satellite or hide them.

## Security

- No new route accepts a filesystem path from the controller. Media is addressed by `(agentId, mediaRef)` only, attachments by bytes only.
- The controller never passes a path that came from a satellite event to a local file, shell or git API (test: a remote event naming `/etc/passwd` or `C:\\Windows` in a file chip produces no local read).

## Acceptance criteria

- Inline images in a remote agent's chat load from the satellite.
- Pasting or dropping an image into a remote chat composer delivers it to the agent on the satellite.
- `clipboard:image` to a chat agent returns an error and leaves no temp file.
- Tests for `mediaRef` validation (traversal, bad refs), the size cap, and the flag gate.

## Dependencies

- #2350 (rich content) for the local feature; #2392, #2393, #2395.
title: [LOW] Annex: rich chat content for remote agents (media by ref, attachments as bytes, no controller-local path reads)
